children.translated_text: I bow to that <s>Adīśvara</s>, by whom the science of <s>haṭhayoga</s> was taught,
as though it were a ladder for one who wishes to ascend to the lofty <s>rājayoga</s>.
Once <s>Caṇḍakāpāli</s>, having gone to the hut of <s>Gheraṇḍa</s>,
bowed with humility and devotion and questioned <s>Gheraṇḍa</s>.
<s>Caṇḍakāpāli</s> said:
O lord of yogins, I now wish to hear the yoga situated in the body, the cause of knowledge of reality.

children.text: idānīṃ śrotum icchāmi yogeśvara vada prabho ||
children.translated_text: O lord of yoga, speak, O master.

children.text: idānīṃ śrotum icchāmi yogeśvara vada prabho ||
children.translated_text: O lord of yoga, speak, O master.
<s>Gheraṇḍa</s> said:

children.text: sādhu sādhu mahābāho yan māṃ tvaṃ paripṛcchasi
children.translated_text: Good, good, mighty-armed one, that you question me thus.
I shall tell you the truth; attend carefully and understand it.

children.text: nāsti māyāsamaḥ pāśo nāsti yogāt paraṃ balam
children.translated_text: There is no snare equal to <s>māyā</s> (illusion), no strength higher than yoga.

children.text: na hi jñānāt paro bandhur nāhaṃkārāt paro ripuḥ ||
children.translated_text: There is no friend higher than knowledge, and no enemy higher than egoism.
Just as, through practice beginning with the letters ka and so on, one may understand the scriptures,

children.text: tathā yogaṃ samāsādya tattvajñānaṃ ca labhyate ||
children.translated_text: so, by attaining yoga, knowledge of reality too is obtained.

children.text: sukṛtair duṣkṛtaiḥ kāryair jāyate prāṇināṃ ghaṭaḥ
children.translated_text: The body of living beings is born from deeds, good and bad.

children.text: ghaṭād utpadyate karma ghaṭayantraṃ yathā bhramet ||
children.translated_text: From the body action arises, as a water-wheel turns.

children.text: ūrdhvādho bhramate yadvad ghaṭayantraṃ gavāṃ vaśāt
children.translated_text: Just as a water-wheel turns upward and downward under the control of oxen,
so the living being, under the control of karma, wanders through birth and death.
The body is always decaying, like an unbaked jar standing in water.
Burning it with the fire of yoga, one should perform purification of the body.

children.text: śodhanaṃ dṛḍhatā caiva sthairyaṃ dhairyaṃ ca lāghavam
children.translated_text: Purification, firmness, steadiness, patience, lightness,

children.text: pratyakṣaṃ ca nirliptaṃ ca ghaṭasthaṃ saptasādhanam ||
children.translated_text: direct perception, and detachment: these are the seven practices belonging to the body.

children.text: ṣaṭkarmaṇā śodhanaṃ ca āsanena bhaved dṛḍham
children.translated_text: Purification is by the six acts, and firmness comes through posture.
Steadiness is by <s>mudrā</s>, and patience by withdrawal of the senses.

children.text: prāṇāyāmāl lāghavaṃ ca dhyānāt pratyakṣam ātmani
children.translated_text: Lightness comes from breath-control, direct perception of the self from meditation,

children.text: samādhinā nirliptaṃ ca muktir eva na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and detachment from <s>samādhi</s>; liberation indeed follows, without doubt.

children.text: dhautir vastis tathā netir laulikī trāṭakaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Dhauti</s>, <s>vasti</s>, <s>neti</s>, <s>laulikī</s>, <s>trāṭaka</s>,
and <s>kapālabhāti</s>: these six acts should be practiced.
Internal cleansing, dental cleansing, heart cleansing, and root purification:

children.text: dhautyaś caturvidhāḥ proktā ghaṭaṃ kurvanti nirmalam ||
children.translated_text: the cleansings are taught as fourfold, and they make the body spotless.
<s>Vātasāra</s>, <s>vārisāra</s>, <s>vahnisāra</s>, and <s>bahiṣkṛta</s>:
for the cleansing of the body, internal <s>dhauti</s> is fourfold.

children.text: kākacañcūvad āsyena pibed vāyuṃ śanaiḥ śanaiḥ
children.translated_text: With the mouth shaped like a crow's beak, one should slowly drink in air,

children.text: cālayed udaraṃ paścād vartmanā recayec chanaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: then move the belly and slowly expel it by the proper channel.
<s>Vātasāra</s> is very secret and causes bodily purification.
It destroys all diseases and increases the body's digestive fire.

children.text: ā kaṇṭhaṃ pūrayed vāri vaktreṇa ca pibec chanaiḥ
children.translated_text: One should fill oneself with water up to the throat, slowly drinking it with the mouth,
move it in the belly, and then expel it downward from the belly.
<s>Vārisāra</s> is very secret and causes bodily purification.
Whoever practices it with effort attains a divine body.

children.text: vārisāraṃ parāṃ dhautiṃ sādhayed yaḥ prayatnataḥ
children.translated_text: Whoever carefully practices <s>vārisāra</s>, the supreme <s>dhauti</s>,
purifies the impure body and attains a divine body.
One should make the navel-knot move against the back of <s>Meru</s> a hundred times.
Abandoning disorders born in the belly, one should increase the gastric fire.
This cleansing is <s>vahnisāra</s>, which grants yogic success to yogins.

children.text: eṣā dhautiḥ parā gopyā na prakāśyā kadācana
children.translated_text: This <s>dhauti</s> is extremely secret and must never be revealed.
By mere <s>dhauti</s> alone, a divine body surely comes about.
Having mastered <s>kākīmudrā</s>, one should fill the great belly,
hold it for half a <s>yāma</s>, and move it by the half-channel.

children.text: eṣā dhautiḥ parā gopyā na prakāśyā kadācana ||
children.translated_text: This <s>dhauti</s> is extremely secret and must never be revealed.
Standing in water up to the navel, one should cleanse the <s>śaktināḍī</s>.
With both hands one should wash the channel until the excrement is discharged.

children.text: tāvat prakṣālya nāḍīṃ ca udare veśayet punaḥ
children.translated_text: Having washed the channel to that extent, one should insert it again into the belly.

children.text: idaṃ prakṣālanaṃ gopyaṃ devānām api durlabham
children.translated_text: This washing is secret, difficult even for the gods to obtain.
By mere <s>dhauti</s> alone, a divine body surely comes about.

children.text: yāmārdhaṃ dhāraṇāśaktiṃ yāvan na sādhayen naraḥ
children.translated_text: So long as a man has not mastered the power of retention for half a <s>yāma</s>,

children.text: bahiṣkṛtaṃ mahādhautī tāvan naiva tu jāyate ||
children.translated_text: so long the great <s>dhauti</s> called <s>bahiṣkṛta</s> does not arise.
The root of the teeth, the root of the tongue, and the openings of the pair of ears,
together with the cranial aperture: these five are prescribed as dental cleansing.
Then, with khadira juice or with pure clay,

children.text: mārjayed dantamūlaṃ ca yāvat kilbiṣam āharet ||
children.translated_text: one should rub the root of the teeth until the impurity is removed.
Cleansing the root of the teeth is the supreme <s>dhauti</s> in the yogins' practice of yoga.

children.text: nityaṃ kuryāt prabhāte ca dantarakṣāya yogavit
children.translated_text: The knower of yoga should do it every morning for the protection of the teeth,
because the root of the teeth is important for yogins in practices such as retention.
Now then I shall explain the means of purifying the tongue.
A long uvula destroys old age, death, diseases, and the like.
Using the three fingers, the index, middle, and ring fingers,
one should insert them into the middle of the throat and rub away the impurity of the uvula.
Rubbing gently again and again, one should remove the disorder of phlegm.

children.text: mārjayen navanītena dohayec ca punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: One should rub it with fresh butter and milk it again and again.
Then, drawing its tip repeatedly with an iron instrument, one should stretch it again and again.
One should do this daily with effort at sunrise and sunset.

children.text: evaṃ kṛte tu nitye ca lambikā dīrghatāṃ gatā ||
children.translated_text: When this is done daily in this way, the uvula becomes long.
With the tip of the index finger one should rub the openings of the ears.
Through constant practice, the inner sound is revealed.
With the right thumb one should rub the opening at the forehead.
By such practice of yoga one should remove the disorder of phlegm.
The channel becomes pure, and divine sight arises.

children.text: nidrānte bhojanānte ca divānte ca dine dine ||
children.translated_text: At the end of sleep, at the end of meals, and at the end of the day, day by day.
One should perform <s>hṛddhauti</s> in three ways: with a stick, with vomiting, and with cloth.
A plantain stalk, a turmeric stalk, and likewise a cane stalk,

children.text: hṛnmadhye cālayitvā tu punaḥ pratyāharec chanaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: having moved it about in the middle of the chest, one should then withdraw it slowly.
He should expel phlegm, bile, and also moisture by the upward path.
By the method of stick-cleansing he will certainly destroy disease of the heart.

children.text: bhojanānte pibed vāri ā karṇapūritaṃ sudhīḥ
children.translated_text: At the end of a meal, the wise man should drink water until it fills up to the ears.

children.text: ūrdhvadṛṣṭiṃ kṣaṇaṃ kṛtvā taj jalaṃ vamayet punaḥ
children.translated_text: Having turned his gaze upward for a moment, he should then vomit that water out.
By the discipline of constant practice one should remove phlegm and bile.
It is nineteen cubits, or else twenty-five,
four finger-breadths wide; one should slowly swallow the fine cloth.
Then one should draw it back out; this is called the act of <s>dhauti</s>.
Abdominal swelling, fever, spleen disease, skin disease, phlegm, and bile are destroyed.

children.text: ārogyaṃ balapuṣṭiś ca bhavet tasya dine dine ||
children.translated_text: Health, strength, and nourishment come to him day by day.

children.text: apānakrūratā tāvad yāvan mūlaṃ na śodhayet
children.translated_text: The harshness of the downward breath remains so long as the root is not cleansed.
Therefore, with every effort, one should practice cleansing of the root.
With a yellow-root stalk, or even with the middle finger,

children.text: yatnena kṣālayed guhyaṃ vāriṇā ca punaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: one should carefully wash the private part again and again with water.
It prevents hardness of the bowels and removes undigested indigestion.
It is the cause of beauty and nourishment, and it kindles the circle of digestive fire.

children.text: jalavastiḥ śuṣkavastir vastī ca dvividhau smṛtau
children.translated_text: <s>Vasti</s> is remembered as twofold: water-vasti and dry-vasti.

children.text: jalavastiṃ jale kuryāc chuṣkavastiṃ kṣitau sadā ||
children.translated_text: One should always perform water-vasti in water, and dry-vasti on the ground.
Having placed the anus in water reaching to the navel, he assumes the squatting posture.
Through contraction and expansion one should perform water-vasti.
It removes urinary disease, rectal obstruction, and harsh wind.
His body becomes free and at ease, and he becomes equal to <s>Kāmadeva</s>.
Having moved the vasti by means of the western stretch, slowly, slowly,
with <s>aśvinīmudrā</s> he should contract and expand the anus.
By such practice of yoga there is no disorder of the bowels.
It increases the gastric fire and destroys <s>āmavāta</s> (rheumatic disorder from undigested matter).
One should insert a fine cord, a span in length, into the nasal passage,
and afterward bring it out through the mouth; this is called the act of <s>neti</s>.
From the performance of the act of neti one may attain success in <s>khecarī</s>.
Disorders of phlegm are destroyed, and divine sight arises.
One should rotate the belly with a strong force on both sides.
Here it destroys all diseases and increases the bodily fire.
Abandoning blinking and opening of the eyes, one should gaze at a subtle target

children.text: yāvad aśru nipatate trāṭakaṃ procyate budhaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: until tears fall; this is called <s>trāṭaka</s> by the wise.
By such practice of yoga, <s>śāṃbhavī</s> surely arises.
Eye disease does not arise; it grants divine sight.
By the left method, the reverse method, and especially the cooling method,
one should perform <s>bhālabhāti</s> in three ways, to remove the disorder of phlegm.

children.text: iḍayā pūrayed vāyuṃ recayet piṅgalā punaḥ
children.translated_text: One should fill the breath through <s>iḍā</s> and then exhale through <s>piṅgalā</s>.
Having filled through <s>piṅgalā</s>, one should again exhale through the moon-channel.

children.text: pūrakaṃ recakaṃ kṛtvā vegena na tu cālayet
children.translated_text: Having performed inhalation and exhalation, one should not move it forcefully.
By such practice of yoga one should remove the disorder of phlegm.

children.text: nāsābhyāṃ jalam ākṛṣya punar vaktreṇa recayet
children.translated_text: Having drawn water in through the two nostrils, one should then expel it through the mouth.

children.text: pāyaṃ pāyaṃ prakurvaṃś cec chleṣmadoṣaṃ nivārayet ||
children.translated_text: If one practices while drinking again and again, one removes the disorder of mucus.
Having sipped with a hissing sound through the mouth, one should expel it through the nasal channels.
By such practice of yoga one becomes equal to <s>Kāmadeva</s>.

children.text: na jāyate vārddhakaṃ ca jvaro naiva prajāyate
children.translated_text: Old age does not arise, nor does fever arise.
The body becomes free and at ease, and one removes the disorder of phlegm.
<s>Gheraṇḍa</s> said:
As many living creatures as there are, so many are all the āsanas.
In ancient times eighty-four lakhs were taught by <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: teṣāṃ madhye viśiṣṭāni ṣoḍaśonaṃ śataṃ kṛtam
children.translated_text: Among them, one hundred less sixteen were made preeminent.

children.text: teṣāṃ madhye martyaloke dvātriṃśad āsanaṃ śubham ||
children.translated_text: Among them, in the mortal world, thirty-two āsanas are auspicious.

children.text: siddhaṃ padmaṃ tathā bhadraṃ muktaṃ vajraṃ ca svastikam
children.translated_text: <s>Siddha</s>, <s>padma</s>, likewise <s>bhadra</s>, <s>mukta</s>, <s>vajra</s>, and <s>svastika</s>,

children.text: siṃhaṃ ca gomukhaṃ vīraṃ dhanurāsanam eva ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>siṃha</s>, <s>gomukha</s>, <s>vīra</s>, and also <s>dhanurāsana</s>,

children.text: mṛtaṃ guptaṃ tathā mātsyaṃ matsyendrāsanam eva ca
children.translated_text: <s>mṛta</s>, <s>gupta</s>, likewise <s>mātsya</s>, and also <s>matsyendrāsana</s>,
<s>gorakṣa</s>, <s>paścimottāna</s>, <s>utkaṭa</s>, and likewise <s>saṃkaṭa</s>,
<s>mayūra</s>, <s>kukkuṭa</s>, <s>kūrma</s>, and likewise <s>uttānakūrmaka</s>,
<s>uttānamaṇḍuka</s>, <s>vṛkṣa</s>, <s>maṇḍūka</s>, <s>garuḍa</s>, and <s>vṛṣa</s>,

children.text: śalabhaṃ makaraṃ coṣṭraṃ bhujaṃgaṃ ca yogāsanam
children.translated_text: <s>śalabha</s>, <s>makara</s>, <s>uṣṭra</s>, <s>bhujaṃga</s>, and <s>yogāsana</s>:

children.text: dvātriṃśad āsanāny eva martyaloke ca siddhidā ||
children.translated_text: these thirty-two āsanas are givers of accomplishment in the mortal world.
Pressing the place of the genitals, with the root of the foot fixed, by the other ankle,

children.text: meḍhropary atha saṃnidhāya cibukaṃ kṛtvā hṛdi sthāpitam
children.translated_text: then placing the penis above it, and setting the chin firmly on the chest,
motionless, with the senses restrained, with an unmoving gaze looking between the eyebrows,
this is called <s>siddhāsana</s>, which breaks open the door-panel of liberation.

children.text: vāmorūpari dakṣiṇaṃ hi caraṇaṃ saṃsthāpya vāmaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Having placed the right foot upon the left thigh, and likewise the left

children.text: dakṣorūpari paścimena vidhinā kṛtvā karābhyāṃ dṛḍham
children.translated_text: upon the right thigh, according to the reverse method, holding them firmly with the two hands,

children.text: aṅguṣṭhau hṛdaye nidhāya cibukaṃ nāsāgram ālokayet
children.translated_text: placing the thumbs at the heart, and with the chin looking at the tip of the nose,
this is called <s>padmāsana</s>, which destroys diseases and disorders.
And the ankles are placed below the testicles, in reverse order and with concentration;

children.text: pādāṅguṣṭhau karābhyāṃ ca dhṛtvā ca pṛṣṭhadeśataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and, from behind the back, he should grasp the big toes with the hands.
Having assumed <s>jālaṃdhara</s>, he should gaze at the tip of the nose.
This is <s>bhadrāsana</s>; it destroys all diseases.
The left ankle is at the root of the anus, and the right ankle likewise above it;
with head, neck, and body aligned, this is <s>muktāsana</s>, which grants accomplishment.

children.text: jaṅghayor vajravat kṛtvā gudapārśve padāv ubhau
children.translated_text: Having made the shanks like a thunderbolt, with both feet beside the anus,
this is <s>vajrāsana</s>, a giver of accomplishment to yogins.

children.text: jānūrvor antare kṛtvā yogī pādatale ubhe
children.translated_text: The yogin places both soles of the feet between the knees and thighs;
seated with the body straight, they call that <s>svastika</s>.
And the ankles, below the testicles, have gone upward in reverse order;
the roots of the soles are set on the ground, and the hands are upon the knees.
With mouth opened, by means of <s>jalandhara</s>, he should gaze at the tip of the nose.
This is <s>siṃhāsana</s>; it destroys all diseases.

children.text: pādau bhūmau ca saṃsthāpya pṛṣṭhapārśve niveśayet
children.translated_text: He should set the feet on the ground and place them at the sides of the back.
Having made the body steady, this is <s>gomukha</s>, shaped like a cow's face.
Then he should place one foot on one thigh,
and afterward similarly on the other; this is called <s>vīrāsana</s>.

children.text: prasārya pādau bhuvi daṇḍarūpau karau ca pṛṣṭhaṃ dhṛtapādayugmam
children.translated_text: Stretching the feet on the ground like staffs, and with the hands behind holding the pair of feet,

children.text: kṛtvā dhanustulyavivartitāṅgaṃ nigadyate vai dhanurāsanaṃ tat ||
children.translated_text: having made the body turned like a bow, that is indeed called <s>dhanurāsana</s>.

children.text: uttānaṃ śavavad bhūmau śayānaṃ tu śavāsanam
children.translated_text: Lying supine on the ground like a corpse is <s>śavāsana</s>.
<s>Śavāsana</s> removes fatigue and is the cause of rest for the mind.

children.text: jānūrvor antare pādau kṛtvā pādau ca gopayet
children.translated_text: Placing the feet between the knees and thighs, and concealing the feet,

children.text: pādopari ca saṃsthāpya gudaṃ guptāsanaṃ viduḥ ||
children.translated_text: and setting the anus upon the feet, they know it as <s>guptāsana</s>.
Having made the free lotus posture, he should lie supine.

children.text: kūrparābhyāṃ śiro veṣṭya matsyāsanaṃ tu rogahā ||
children.translated_text: Enclosing the head with the elbows, <s>matsyāsana</s> removes disease.

children.text: udare paścimaṃ tānaṃ kṛtvā tiṣṭhati yatnataḥ
children.translated_text: Having made a western stretch in the belly, he remains with effort.
With the body bent, he should place the left foot upon the right knee.

children.text: tatra yāmyaṃ kūrparaṃ ca yāmyakare ca vaktrakam
children.translated_text: There the right elbow, and the face in the right hand,

children.text: bhruvor madhye gatā dṛṣṭiḥ pīṭhaṃ matsyendram ucyate ||
children.translated_text: with the gaze gone to the space between the brows: this seat is called <s>matsyendra</s>.
The feet are placed between the knees and thighs, turned upward and clearly set;
covering the ankles carefully with both upturned hands,
having contracted the throat, he should gaze at the tip of the nose.
They call this <s>gorakṣāsana</s>, the cause of accomplishment for yogins.

children.text: prasārya pādau bhuvi daṇḍarūpau saṃnyastabhālaṃ citiyugmamadhye
children.translated_text: Stretching the feet on the ground like staffs, with the forehead placed between the pair of shanks,

children.text: yatnena pādau ca dhṛtau karābhyāṃ yogendrapīṭhaṃ paścimatānam āhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the feet carefully held by the hands, the lords of yoga call this seat <s>paścimatāna</s>.

children.text: aṅguṣṭhābhyām avaṣṭabhya dharāṃ gulphau ca khe gatau
children.translated_text: Supporting himself on the ground with the big toes, while the ankles have gone into the air,
he should place the anus above them; this is to be understood as <s>utkaṭāsana</s>.
Setting the root of the left foot's sole on the ground,
he should wrap the left foot with the staff-like right foot.
The pair of hands is on the pair of knees: this is the difficult posture, <s>saṃkaṭāsana</s>.

children.text: dharām avaṣṭabhya karadvayābhyāṃ tat kūrpare sthāpitanābhipārśvam
children.translated_text: Supporting the ground with the two hands, with the region of the navel set upon the elbows,

children.text: uccāsane daṇḍavad utthitaḥ khe mayūram etat pravadanti pīṭham ||
children.translated_text: raised in the air like a staff on a high seat: they call this the <s>mayūra</s> seat.

children.text: bahukadaśanabhuktaṃ bhasma kuryād aśeṣaṃ janayati jaṭharāgniṃ jārayet kālakūṭam
children.translated_text: It reduces to ashes all food eaten in excess, kindles the digestive fire, and digests even <s>kālakūṭa</s> poison.

children.text: harati sakalarogān āśu gulmajvarādīn bhavati vigatadoṣaṃ hy āsanaṃ śrīmayūram ||
children.translated_text: It quickly removes all diseases, such as abdominal tumors and fevers; indeed the glorious <s>mayūra</s> posture becomes free from faults.
Having assumed <s>padmāsana</s>, with the hands between the knees and thighs,
seated on the elbows as if on a couch: this is <s>kukkuṭāsana</s>.
The ankles are placed below the testicles in reverse order;
with body, head, and neck straight, this is called <s>kūrmāsana</s>.
Being in the bind of <s>kukkuṭāsana</s>, with the neck held by the hands,
supine like a sky-tortoise: this is <s>uttānakūrmakam</s>.

children.text: pādatalau pṛṣṭhadeśe aṅguṣṭhau dvau ca saṃspṛśet
children.translated_text: He should touch the soles of the feet on the back, and also the two big toes,
bringing the pair of knees forward; he should accomplish <s>maṇḍūkāsana</s>.
Being in the bind of <s>maṇḍūkāsana</s>, with the head held by the elbows,
this supine form like a frog is <s>uttānamaṇḍukam</s>.

children.text: vāmorumūladeśe ca yāmyaṃ pādaṃ nidhāya tu
children.translated_text: Placing the right foot at the root-region of the left thigh,

children.text: tiṣṭhati vṛkṣavad bhūmau vṛkṣāsanam idaṃ viduḥ ||
children.translated_text: he stands on the ground like a tree; this they know as <s>vṛkṣāsana</s>.
Pressing the ground with shanks and thighs, with body steady and with the two knees,
the pair of hands upon the knees: this is called <s>garuḍāsana</s>.
The root of the anus is at the right ankle, and the other foot is on the left side;

children.text: viparītaṃ spṛśed bhūmiṃ vṛṣāsanam idaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: touching the ground in the reverse way, this becomes <s>vṛṣāsana</s>.

children.text: adhyāsya śete padayugmavakṣe bhūmim avaṣṭabhya karadvayābhyām
children.translated_text: Lying face down, with the pair of feet on the chest, supporting the ground with the two hands,

children.text: pādau ca śūnye ca vitasti cordhvaṃ vadanti pīṭhaṃ śalabhaṃ munīndrāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the feet in the empty air a span upward: the great sages call this seat <s>śalabha</s>.

children.text: adhyāsya śete hṛdayaṃ nidhāya bhūmau ca pādau pravisāryamāṇau
children.translated_text: Lying face down, placing the heart on the ground, and with the feet being stretched out,

children.text: śiraś ca dhṛtvā karadaṇḍayugme dehāgnikāraṃ makarāsanaṃ tat ||
children.translated_text: and holding the head on the pair of staff-like arms: that fire-making posture of the body is <s>makarāsana</s>.

children.text: adhyāsya śete padayugmam astaṃ pṛṣṭhe nidhāyāpi dhṛtaṃ karābhyām
children.translated_text: Lying face down, with the pair of feet set behind, and held by the hands,

children.text: ākuñcya samyagghyudarāsyagaṇḍam uṣṭraṃ ca pīṭhaṃ yatayo vadanti ||
children.translated_text: properly contracting the belly, mouth, and cheeks: ascetics call this seat <s>uṣṭra</s>.
He should place the lower part of the body on the ground up to the navel and big toes,

children.text: karatalābhyāṃ dharāṃ dhṛtvā ūrdhvaṃ śīrṣaṃ phaṇīva hi ||
children.translated_text: holding the earth with the palms, and raising the head upward like a serpent's hood.
The bodily fire constantly increases; it destroys all diseases.
Through practice the divine serpent-power awakens; this is <s>bhujaṅgāsana</s>.
Having made the feet face upward, one should place them above the knees,
and, seated upon the seat, place the pair of hands turned upward.
Drawing in the breath with inhalations, one should gaze at the tip of the nose.
This becomes the yogic posture for yogins in the practice of yoga.
<s>Gheraṇḍa</s> said:
<s>Mahāmudrā</s>, <s>nabhomudrā</s>, <s>uḍḍīyāna</s>, <s>jalaṃdhara</s>,
<s>mūlabandha</s>, <s>mahābandha</s>, <s>mahāvedha</s>, and <s>khecarī</s>,
<s>viparītakaraṇī</s>, <s>yoni</s>, <s>vajrolī</s>, <s>śakticālanī</s>,
<s>taḍāgī</s>, <s>māṇḍukī</s>, <s>śāmbhavī</s>, and the fivefold concentration,

children.text: aśvinī pāśinī kākī mātaṃgī ca bhujaṅginī
children.translated_text: <s>aśvinī</s>, <s>pāśinī</s>, <s>kākī</s>, <s>mātaṃgī</s>, and <s>bhujaṅginī</s>:
these twenty-five mudrās here bestow siddhi upon yogins.

children.text: mudrāṇāṃ paṭalaṃ devi kathitaṃ tava saṃnidhau
children.translated_text: O goddess, the chapter on the mudrās has been taught in your presence;
by the mere knowledge of it, every siddhi arises.

children.text: gopanīyaṃ prayatnena na deyaṃ yasya kasyacit
children.translated_text: It is to be carefully kept secret; it is not to be given to just anyone.

children.text: prītidaṃ yogināṃ caiva durlabhaṃ marutām api ||
children.translated_text: It gives delight to yogins, and is hard to obtain even for the gods.
Pressing the root of the anus firmly with the left ankle, with steady effort,
then stretching out the right foot and holding the toes with the two hands,
contracting the throat, one should gaze between the eyebrows.
Filling the air by inhalations, this is called <s>mahāmudrā</s>.

children.text: valitaṃ palitaṃ caiva jarāṃ mṛtyuṃ nivārayet
children.translated_text: It prevents wrinkles, grey hair, old age, and death.
Consumption, cough, rectal obstruction, spleen disease, indigestion, and fever as well,
and all diseases are destroyed by the practice of <s>mahāmudrā</s>.

children.text: yatra yatra sthito yogī sarvakāryeṣu sarvadā
children.translated_text: Wherever a yogin is situated, in all activities and at all times,

children.text: ūrdhvajihvaḥ sthiro bhūtvā dhārayet pavanaṃ sadā
children.translated_text: having become steady with the tongue turned upward, he should always hold the breath.
This is <s>nabhomudrā</s>, which destroys disease for yogins.

children.text: udare paścimaṃ tānaṃ nābher ūrdhvaṃ tu kārayet
children.translated_text: One should make a western stretch in the belly above the navel.
Because the great bird flies upward unceasingly from it,
that bandha is <s>uḍḍīyāna</s>, the lion against the elephant of death.
Because of the complete binding, this <s>uḍḍīyāna</s> is distinguished.
When <s>uḍḍīyāna</s> is well practiced, liberation becomes natural.
Contracting the throat, one should place the chin on the heart.
When the <s>jālaṃdhara</s> bandha is made, it binds the sixteen supports.
The great mudrā <s>jālaṃdhara</s> brings about the destruction of death.
The perfected <s>jālaṃdhara</s> bandha bestows siddhi upon yogins.

children.text: ṣaṇmāsam abhyased yo hi sa siddho nātra saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He who practices it for six months becomes perfected; there is no doubt here.
Then with the heel of the left foot one should contract the yoni,
and the wise man should carefully press the navel-knot against the spinal staff.
With the right ankle he should make a firm binding of the penis.

children.text: nābher ūrdhvam adhaś cāpi tānaṃ kuryāt prayatnataḥ
children.translated_text: He should carefully make a stretch both above and below the navel.
The mudrā that destroys old age is called <s>mūlabandha</s>.
The man who desires to cross the ocean of saṃsāra

children.text: virale sugupto bhūtvā mudrām etāṃ samabhyaset ||
children.translated_text: should become well concealed in a solitary place and practice this mudrā.
From practice of this bandha, mastery of the vital wind surely arises.

children.text: sādhayed yatnatas tarhi maunī tu vijitālasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore he should accomplish it with effort, silent and having conquered laziness.
With the ankle of the left foot he should restrain the root of the anus.

children.text: dakṣapādena tad gulphaṃ saṃpīḍya yatnataḥ sudhīḥ ||
children.translated_text: With the right foot, the wise man should carefully press that ankle.

children.text: śanaiḥ śanaiś cālayet pārṣṇiṃ yonim ākuñcayec chanaiḥ
children.translated_text: Slowly, slowly he should move the heel and slowly contract the yoni.
He should hold the breath in <s>jālaṃdhara</s>; this is called <s>mahābandha</s>.
<s>Mahābandha</s> is the supreme bandha, destroying old age and death.
By the favor of this bandha, one accomplishes everything desired.
Beauty, youth, and loveliness are fruitless for women without a man;
so too <s>mūlabandha</s> and <s>mahābandha</s> are fruitless without <s>mahāvedha</s>.
Having attained <s>mahābandha</s>, one should perform <s>uḍḍāna</s> kumbhaka.
This is called <s>mahāvedha</s>, bestowing siddhi upon yogins.
Whoever performs <s>mahābandha</s> and <s>mūlabandha</s> together with <s>mahāvedha</s>

children.text: pratyahaṃ kurute yas tu sa yogī yogavittamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: every day is a yogin, the best knower of yoga.

children.text: na mṛtyuto bhayaṃ tasya na jarā tasya vidyate
children.translated_text: For him there is no fear of death, and for him there is no old age.
This <s>vedha</s> is to be carefully kept secret by the foremost yogins.

children.text: jihvādho nāḍīṃ saṃchitya rasanāṃ cālayet sadā
children.translated_text: Having cut the channel beneath the tongue, one should always move the tongue.
One should milk it with fresh butter and draw it out with an iron instrument.
By such constant practice, the uvula-region gains length.

children.text: yāvad gacched bhruvor madhye tadā sidhyati khecarī ||
children.translated_text: When it reaches between the eyebrows, then <s>khecarī</s> is perfected.

children.text: rasanāṃ tālumadhye tu śanaiḥ śanaiḥ praveśayet
children.translated_text: One should slowly, slowly insert the tongue into the middle of the palate.
When the tongue, turned backward, has entered the cavity of the skull,

children.text: bhruvor madhye gatā dṛṣṭir mudrā bhavati khecarī ||
children.translated_text: and the gaze has gone between the eyebrows, the mudrā is <s>khecarī</s>.

children.text: na ca mūrchā kṣudhā tṛṣṇā naivālasyaṃ prajāyate
children.translated_text: Fainting, hunger, thirst, and laziness do not arise,

children.text: na ca rogo jarā mṛtyur devadehaṃ prapadyate ||
children.translated_text: nor disease, old age, or death; one obtains a divine body.

children.text: na cāgnir dahate gātraṃ na śoṣayati mārutaḥ
children.translated_text: Fire does not burn the limbs, nor does wind dry them out.

children.text: na dehaṃ kledayanty āpo daṃśayen na bhujaṃgamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Waters do not moisten the body, nor can a serpent bite it.

children.text: lāvaṇyaṃ ca bhaved gātre samādhir jāyate dhruvam
children.translated_text: Loveliness arises in the body, and samādhi surely arises.
When the tongue joins with the cranial opening, the tongue obtains rasa.
Day by day, various kinds of bliss arise from it.
At first there is salty and alkaline taste, then bitter and astringent.
Then there are fresh butter, ghee, milk, curds, buttermilk, and honey,
grape juice and nectar; such tongue-water arises.

children.text: nābhimūle vaset sūryas tālumūle ca candramāḥ
children.translated_text: The sun abides at the root of the navel, and the moon at the root of the palate.

children.text: amṛtaṃ grasate sūryas tato mṛtyuvaśo naraḥ ||
children.translated_text: The sun devours the nectar; therefore a person comes under the power of death.

children.text: ūrdhvaṃ ca yojayet sūryaṃ candraṃ ca adha ānayet
children.translated_text: One should direct the sun upward and bring the moon downward.
The <s>viparītakarī mudrā</s> is kept secret in all tantras.

children.text: bhūmau śiraś ca saṃsthāpya karayugmaṃ samāhitaḥ
children.translated_text: Having placed the head on the ground, with the pair of hands composed,
and having become steady with the feet upward, this is regarded as <s>viparītakarī</s>.

children.text: mudreyaṃ sādhayen nityaṃ jarāṃ mṛtyuṃ ca nāśayet
children.translated_text: One should practice this <s>mudrā</s> daily; it destroys old age and death.

children.text: sa siddhaḥ sarvalokeṣu pralaye 'pi na sīdati ||
children.translated_text: He is perfected among all people and does not sink even at the dissolution.
Having assumed <s>siddhāsana</s>, he should hold the ears, eyes, nose, and mouth
with the thumbs, index fingers, middle fingers, ring fingers, and the rest.

children.text: kākībhiḥ prāṇaṃ saṃkṛṣya apāne yojayet tataḥ
children.translated_text: Drawing in the breath with a crow-like beak, he should then join it with <s>apāna</s>.

children.text: ṣaṭ cakrāṇi kramād dhṛtvā huṃhaṃsamanunā sudhīḥ ||
children.translated_text: The wise man should hold the six <s>cakras</s> in sequence with the mantra <s>huṃ haṃsa</s>.

children.text: caitanyam ānayed devīṃ nidritā yā bhujaṅginī
children.translated_text: He should bring to consciousness the goddess, the sleeping serpent-woman,
and, raising the <s>śakti</s> together with the living soul, into the supreme lotus,

children.text: śaktimayaṃ svayaṃ bhūtvā paraṃ śivena saṃgamam
children.translated_text: having himself become made of <s>śakti</s>, he should contemplate union with supreme <s>Śiva</s>,

children.text: nānāsukhaṃ vihāraṃ ca cintayet paramaṃ sukham ||
children.translated_text: varied pleasure and sport, and the highest bliss.
From the union of <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Śakti</s> he should meditate on solitude upon the earth.
Having a mind full of bliss, he should come to be, 'I am <s>Brahman</s>.'

children.text: yonimudrā parā gopyā devānām api durlabhā
children.translated_text: The <s>yonimudrā</s> is supremely secret, hard to obtain even for the gods.

children.text: sakṛt tadbhāvasaṃsiddhaḥ samādhisthaḥ sa eva hi ||
children.translated_text: He who has attained perfection in that state even once is indeed established in <s>samādhi</s>.
A killer of a brahmin, a killer of an embryo, a drinker of liquor, and one who has gone to the teacher's bed,
is not tainted by these sins because of the binding of <s>yonimudrā</s>.

children.text: yāni pāpāni ghorāṇi upapāpāni yāni ca
children.translated_text: Whatever terrible sins there are, and whatever secondary sins there are,
all those perish because of the binding of <s>yonimudrā</s>.

children.text: tasmād abhyasanaṃ kuryād yadi muktiṃ samicchati ||
children.translated_text: Therefore one should perform its practice if one desires liberation.

children.text: dharām avaṣṭabhya karadvayābhyām ūrdhvaṃ kṣipet pādayugaṃ śiraḥ khe
children.translated_text: Supporting the earth with the two hands, he should throw the pair of feet upward, with the head in the air.
For the awakening of <s>śakti</s> and for long life, the sages call this <s>vajrolīmudrā</s>.
This yoga is the best of yogas, the cause of liberation for yogins.
This beneficial yoga grants accomplishment to yogins.
By the favor of this yoga, mastery of <s>bindu</s> surely arises.

children.text: siddhe bindau mahāyatne kiṃ na sidhyati bhūtale ||
children.translated_text: When <s>bindu</s> is mastered through great effort, what is not accomplished on earth?

children.text: bhogena mahatā yukto yadi mudrāṃ samācaret
children.translated_text: Even if one is joined with great enjoyment, if he practices the <s>mudrā</s>,

children.text: tathāpi sakalā siddhis tasya bhavati niścitam ||
children.translated_text: then surely every accomplishment becomes his.
In the <s>mūlādhāra</s> is the self-power, <s>Kuṇḍalī</s>, the supreme goddess.
She lies in the form of a serpent, furnished with three and a half coils.

children.text: yāvat sā nidritā dehe tāvaj jīvaḥ paśur yathā
children.translated_text: So long as she sleeps in the body, the living being is like an animal.

children.text: jñānaṃ na jāyate tāvat koṭiyogaṃ samabhyaset ||
children.translated_text: So long knowledge does not arise, even though he practice ten million yogas.

children.text: udghāṭayet kavāṭaṃ ca yathā kuñcikayā haṭhāt
children.translated_text: Just as one forcibly opens a door with a key,
so by the awakening of <s>Kuṇḍalinī</s> one should pierce the door of <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: nābhiṃ bṛhad veṣṭanaṃ ca na ca nagnaṃ bahiḥ sthitam
children.translated_text: With the navel well wrapped, not naked and not standing outside,
one should remain in a secret house and practice <s>śakticālana</s>.
An upper garment is said to be a span long, four fingers in breadth,
soft, white, fine, and suitable for wrapping.

children.text: evam ambaram uktaṃ ca kaṭisūtreṇa yojayet ||
children.translated_text: Such a cloth has been described, and one should fasten it with a waist-cord.
With the limbs smeared with ash, he should practice <s>siddhāsana</s>.

children.text: nāsābhyāṃ prāṇam ākṛṣya apāne yojayed balāt ||
children.translated_text: Drawing breath through the nostrils, he should forcefully join it with <s>apāna</s>.
He should contract the anus gently by <s>aśvinīmudrā</s>,
until the wind goes into the <s>suṣumṇā</s> and forcibly makes it manifest.
Then, through the piercing by the wind, the serpent-woman and the little pot

children.text: baddhaśvāsas tato bhūtvā ca ūrdhvamātraṃ prapadyate
children.translated_text: become held in the breath, and she then proceeds only upward.

children.text: śabdadvayaṃ phalaikaṃ tu yonimudrāṃ ca cālayet ||
children.translated_text: The two sounds have one result; and he should set <s>yonimudrā</s> in motion.
Without the movement of <s>śakti</s>, <s>yonimudrā</s> is not perfected.
First practicing the movement, one should practice <s>yonimudrā</s> thoroughly.

children.text: iti te kathitaṃ caṇḍa prakāraṃ śakticālanam
children.translated_text: Thus, O <s>Caṇḍa</s>, the method of moving <s>śakti</s> has been told to you.
It is to be carefully kept secret and practiced day by day.
This <s>mudrā</s> is supremely secret and destroys old age and death.
Therefore practice should be undertaken by yogins who desire accomplishment.

children.text: nityaṃ yo 'bhyasate yogī siddhis tasya kare sthitā
children.translated_text: For the yogin who practices daily, accomplishment stands in his hand.

children.text: tasya vigrahasiddhiḥ syād rogāṇāṃ saṃkṣayo bhavet ||
children.translated_text: He obtains perfection of the body, and the destruction of diseases comes about.

children.text: udare paścimaṃ tānaṃ kṛtvā ca taḍāgākṛti
children.translated_text: Having made a western stretch in the belly, in the form of a pond,
that is the supreme <s>taḍāgī mudrā</s>, destroyer of old age and death.
Having closed the mouth, he should move the root of the tongue.

children.text: śanair grased amṛtaṃ tan māṇḍukīṃ mudrikāṃ viduḥ ||
children.translated_text: He should slowly swallow that nectar; they know this as <s>māṇḍukī mudrā</s>.
Wrinkles and grayness do not arise; there is perpetual youth.

children.text: na keśe jāyate pāko yaḥ kuryān nityamāṇḍukīm ||
children.translated_text: There is no ripening in the hair for one who performs <s>māṇḍukī</s> daily.
Looking at the collyrium of the eyes, he should behold the self-delighting one.

children.text: sā bhavec chāmbhavī mudrā sarvatantreṣu gopitā ||
children.translated_text: That is the <s>śāmbhavī mudrā</s>, kept secret in all tantras.
The Vedas, śāstras, and purāṇas are like common courtesans;

children.text: iyaṃ tu śāmbhavī mudrā guptā kulavadhūr iva ||
children.translated_text: but this <s>śāmbhavī mudrā</s> is hidden like a noble family's wife.

children.text: sa eva ādināthaś ca sa ca nārāyaṇaḥ svayam
children.translated_text: He himself is <s>Ādinātha</s>, and he is <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> himself;

children.text: sa ca brahmā sṛṣṭikārī yo mudrāṃ vetti śāmbhavīm ||
children.translated_text: he is <s>Brahmā</s>, the creator, who knows the <s>śāmbhavī mudrā</s>.

children.text: satyaṃ satyaṃ punaḥ satyaṃ satyam uktaṃ maheśvara
children.translated_text: Truth, truth, again truth; truth has been spoken, O <s>Maheśvara</s>.

children.text: śāmbhavīṃ yo vijānīyāt sa ca brahma na cānyathā ||
children.translated_text: Whoever knows <s>śāmbhavī</s> is <s>Brahman</s>, and not otherwise.
The <s>śāmbhavī mudrā</s> has been described; listen to the five concentrations.

children.text: dhāraṇāni samāsādya kiṃ na sidhyati bhūtale ||
children.translated_text: Having mastered the concentrations, what is not accomplished on earth?
With this human body, going and coming in the heavens

children.text: manogatir bhavet tasya khecaratvaṃ na cānyathā ||
children.translated_text: and movement at the speed of thought become his; so too sky-going, and not otherwise.

children.text: yat tattvaṃ haritāladeśaracitaṃ bhaumaṃ lakārānvitaṃ vedāsraṃ kamalāsanena sahitaṃ kṛtvā hṛdi sthāyinam
children.translated_text: Having made that earth element, prepared in the region of yellow orpiment, accompanied by the syllable <s>la</s>, four-sided, and together with the lotus-seated one, fixed in the heart,

children.text: prāṇaṃ tatra vinīya pañcaghaṭikāś cittānvitaṃ dhārayed eṣā stambhakarī sadā kṣitijayaṃ kuryād adhodhāraṇā ||
children.translated_text: he should lead the breath there and hold it, joined with the mind, for five ghaṭikās. This is the downward dhāraṇā, which brings about steadiness and always grants mastery over earth.
He who regularly performs the mudrā of the earthly dhāraṇā,

children.text: mṛtyuṃjayaḥ svayaṃ so 'pi sa siddho vicared bhuvi ||
children.translated_text: he himself becomes a conqueror of death; as an accomplished one he moves about on the earth.

children.text: śaṅkhendupratimaṃ ca kundadhavalaṃ tattvaṃ kilālaṃ śubhaṃ tat pīyūṣavakārabījasahitaṃ yuktaṃ sadā viṣṇunā
children.translated_text: The water element, auspicious, resembling a conch and the moon, white as jasmine, together with the nectarous seed-syllable <s>va</s> and always joined with <s>Viṣṇu</s>,

children.text: prāṇaṃ tatra vinīya pañcaghaṭikāś cittānvitaṃ dhārayed eṣā duḥsahatāpapāpaharaṇī syād āmbhasī dhāraṇā ||
children.translated_text: he should lead the breath there and hold it, joined with the mind, for five ghaṭikās. This is the watery dhāraṇā, which removes unbearable heat and sin.

children.text: āmbhasīṃ paramāṃ mudrāṃ yo jānāti sa yogavit
children.translated_text: He who knows the supreme watery mudrā is a knower of yoga.

children.text: jale ca gabhīre ghore maraṇaṃ tasya no bhavet ||
children.translated_text: Even in deep and terrible water, death will not befall him.

children.text: iyaṃ tu paramā mudrā gopanīyā prayatnataḥ
children.translated_text: But this is a supreme mudrā, to be carefully kept secret.

children.text: prakāśāt siddhihāniḥ syāt satyaṃ vacmi ca tattvataḥ ||
children.translated_text: If it is revealed, there will be loss of accomplishment; I speak the truth, exactly as it is.

children.text: yan nābhisthitam indragopasadṛśaṃ bījatrikoṇānvitaṃ tattvaṃ tejomayaṃ pradīptam aruṇaṃ rudreṇa yat siddhidam
children.translated_text: That fire element, situated at the navel, like an indragopa insect, endowed with the triangular seed, radiant, blazing, red, and granting accomplishment with <s>Rudra</s>,

children.text: prāṇaṃ tatra vinīya pañcaghaṭikāś cittānvitaṃ dhārayed eṣā kālagabhīrabhītiharaṇī vaiśvānarī dhāraṇā ||
children.translated_text: he should lead the breath there and hold it, joined with the mind, for five ghaṭikās. This is the fiery dhāraṇā, which removes fear of the deep abyss of time and death.

children.text: pradīpte jvalite vahnau yadi patati sādhakaḥ
children.translated_text: If the practitioner falls into a blazing, burning fire,
by the favor of this mudrā he lives and does not become subject to death.

children.text: yad bhinnāñjanapuñjasaṃnibham idaṃ dhūmrāvabhāsaṃ paraṃ tattvaṃ sattvamayaṃ yakārasahitaṃ yatreśvaro devatā
children.translated_text: This supreme element, resembling a mass of split collyrium, smoky in appearance, consisting of sattva, accompanied by the syllable <s>ya</s>, where <s>Īśvara</s> is the deity,

children.text: prāṇaṃ tatra vinīya pañcaghaṭikāś cittānvitaṃ dhārayed eṣā khe gamanaṃ karoti yamināṃ syād vāyavī dhāraṇā ||
children.translated_text: he should lead the breath there and hold it, joined with the mind, for five ghaṭikās. This is the airy dhāraṇā, which gives disciplined yogins movement in the sky.
But this is a supreme mudrā, destroying old age and death.

children.text: vāyunā mriyate nāpi khe ca gatipradāyinī ||
children.translated_text: Nor does one die through wind; and it grants movement in the sky.

children.text: śaṭhāya bhaktihīnāya na deyā yasya kasyacit
children.translated_text: It should not be given to a rogue, to one without devotion, or to just anyone at all.

children.text: datte ca siddhihāniḥ syāt satyaṃ vacmi ca caṇḍa te ||
children.translated_text: If it is given, there will be loss of accomplishment; I speak the truth, <s>Caṇḍa</s>.

children.text: yat sindhau varaśuddhavārisadṛśaṃ vyomaṃ paraṃ bhāsitaṃ tattvaṃ devasadāśivena sahitaṃ bījaṃ hakārānvitam
children.translated_text: The space element, supreme, shining like excellent pure water in the ocean, together with the god <s>Sadāśiva</s>, and the seed accompanied by the syllable <s>ha</s>,

children.text: prāṇaṃ tatra vinīya pañcaghaṭikāś cittānvitaṃ dhārayed eṣā mokṣakavāṭabhedanakarī tu syān nabhodhāraṇā ||
children.translated_text: he should lead the breath there and hold it, joined with the mind, for five ghaṭikās. This is the ethereal dhāraṇā, which breaks open the door of liberation.

children.text: ākāśīdhāraṇāṃ mudrāṃ yo vetti sa ca yogavit
children.translated_text: He who knows the mudrā of the space dhāraṇā is a knower of yoga.

children.text: na mṛtyur jāyate tasya pralaye nāvasīdati ||
children.translated_text: Death does not arise for him; even at dissolution he does not sink down.
One should contract the anal aperture and release it again and again.
That is <s>aśvinī mudrā</s>, which awakens the śakti.
<s>Aśvinī</s> is a supreme mudrā, destroying diseases of the private parts,
giving strength and nourishment, and removing untimely death.
One should throw the feet behind the neck, making a firm binding like a noose.
That indeed is <s>pāśinī mudrā</s>, which awakens the śakti.
<s>Pāśinī</s> is a great mudrā, bestowing strength and nourishment.
It should be practiced carefully by practitioners who desire accomplishment.

children.text: kākacañcuvad āsyena pibed vāyuṃ śanaiḥ śanaiḥ
children.translated_text: With the mouth like a crow's beak, one should slowly drink in air.
This is <s>kākī mudrā</s>, destroying all diseases.
<s>Kākī mudrā</s> is a supreme mudrā, kept secret in all tantras.

children.text: asyāḥ prasādamātreṇa na rogī kākavad bhavet ||
children.translated_text: By merely obtaining its favor, one does not become diseased, and becomes like a crow.
Standing in water up to the throat, one should draw in water through the nostrils,

children.text: mukhān nirgamayet paścāt punar vaktreṇa cāharet ||
children.translated_text: then expel it through the mouth, and afterward draw it in again through the mouth.

children.text: nāsābhyāṃ recayet paścāt kuryād evaṃ punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: Then one should expel it through the nostrils; one should do this again and again.
<s>Mātaṃginī</s> is a supreme mudrā, destroying old age and death.
Staying in a solitary, unfrequented place, with mind one-pointed,

children.text: kuryān mātaṃginīṃ mudrāṃ mātaṃga iva jāyate ||
children.translated_text: one should perform <s>mātaṃginī mudrā</s>; he becomes like an elephant.

children.text: yatra yatra sthito yogī sukham atyantam aśnute
children.translated_text: Wherever the yogin stays, he experiences the utmost happiness.
Therefore, by every effort, one should master the supreme mudrā.

children.text: vaktraṃ kiṃcit suprasārya cālinaṃ galayā pibet
children.translated_text: Opening the mouth somewhat, one should drink in air through the throat.
That is <s>bhujagī mudrā</s>, destroying old age and death.

children.text: yāvac ca udare rogam ajīrṇādi viśeṣataḥ
children.translated_text: Whatever disease is in the belly, especially indigestion and the like,

children.text: tat sarvaṃ nāśayed āśu yatra mudrā bhujaṅginī ||
children.translated_text: all that the mudrā <s>bhujaṅginī</s> quickly destroys.

children.text: idaṃ tu mudrāpaṭalaṃ kathitaṃ caṇḍa te śubham
children.translated_text: This auspicious chapter on mudrās has been told to you, <s>Caṇḍa</s>.
It is beloved of all accomplished beings and destroys old age and death.

children.text: śaṭhāya bhaktihīnāya na deyaṃ yasya kasyacit
children.translated_text: It should not be given to a rogue, to one without devotion, or to just anyone at all.
It is to be carefully kept secret, difficult even for the gods of wind to obtain.
It should be given to one who is upright, peaceful in mind, and devoted above all to the guru,
to one of good family; it grants both enjoyment and liberation.
This chapter on the mudrās destroys all diseases,
and, for one whose nature is constant practice, increases the digestive fire.

children.text: na tasya jāyate mṛtyur nāsya jarādikaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Death does not arise for him, nor does old age and the like.

children.text: nāgnijalabhayaṃ tasya vāyor api kuto bhayam ||
children.translated_text: For him there is no fear of fire or water; how then could there be fear even of wind?

children.text: kāsaḥ śvāsaḥ plīhā kuṣṭhaṃ śleṣmarogāś ca viṃśatiḥ
children.translated_text: Cough, asthma, spleen disease, skin disease, and the twenty phlegmatic disorders

children.text: mudrāṇāṃ sādhanāc caiva vinaśyanti na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: are destroyed by the practice of mudrās; there is no doubt.

children.text: bahunā kim ihoktena sāraṃ vacmi ca caṇḍa te
children.translated_text: What need is there of much speech here? I tell you the essence, <s>Caṇḍa</s>:
there is nothing on the surface of the earth equal to mudrā for giving accomplishment.
<s>Gheraṇḍa</s> said:
Now then I shall fully teach the excellent practice of pratyāhāra,
by the mere knowledge of which the enemies beginning with desire are destroyed.

children.text: yato yato niścarati manaś cañcalam asthiram
children.translated_text: Wherever the restless, unstable mind goes out,

children.text: tatas tato niyamyaitad ātmany eva vaśaṃ nayet ||
children.translated_text: from there and there one should restrain it and bring it under control in the self alone.

children.text: yatra yatra gatā dṛṣṭir manas tatra pragacchati
children.translated_text: Wherever the gaze has gone, the mind proceeds there.

children.text: tataḥ pratyāhared etad ātmany eva vaśaṃ nayet ||
children.translated_text: Therefore one should withdraw it and bring it under control in the self alone.
Whether honor or insult, whether something pleasant to hear or terrifying,

children.text: manas tasmān niyamyaitad ātmanyeva vaśaṃ nayet ||
children.translated_text: one should restrain the mind from that and bring it under control in the self alone.

children.text: śītaṃ vāpi tathā coṣṇaṃ yan manaḥsparśayogataḥ
children.translated_text: Whether cold or also heat, when it is connected with contact of the mind,

children.text: tasmāt pratyāhared etad ātmany eva vaśaṃ nayet ||
children.translated_text: one should withdraw it from that and bring it under control in the self alone.

children.text: sugandhe vāpi durgandhe ghrāṇeṣu jāyate manaḥ
children.translated_text: When the mind arises in the nose with respect to fragrance or foul odor,

children.text: tasmāt pratyāhared etad ātmany eva vaśaṃ nayet ||
children.translated_text: one should withdraw it from that and bring it under control in the self alone.
When the mind has gone to tastes such as sweet, sour, pungent, and bitter,

children.text: tasmāt pratyāhared etad ātmany eva vaśaṃ nayet ||
children.translated_text: one should withdraw it from that and bring it under control in the self alone.
The knower of yoga, devoted to <s>pratyāhāra</s> (sense withdrawal), should restrain the senses attached to sound and the other objects,
and make them follow the mind.
Through that, supreme controllability arises for the very restless senses.

children.text: indriyāṇām avaśyais tair na yogī yogasādhakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: With those senses uncontrolled, a yogin is not one who accomplishes yoga.

children.text: prāṇāyāmair dahed doṣān dhāraṇābhiś ca kilbiṣam
children.translated_text: By <s>prāṇāyāma</s> (breath control) one should burn up faults, and by concentrations, sin;
by <s>pratyāhāra</s>, the sense objects, and by meditation, the qualities that are not the Lord.
Just as the impurities of mountain ores are burned away when they are smelted,
so faults produced by the senses are burned away through restraint of breath.

children.text: samaḥ samāsano bhūtvā saṃhṛtya caraṇāv ubhau
children.translated_text: Having become even, seated in an even posture, and having drawn in both feet,
with the mouth closed, likewise properly bracing the thighs in front,
not touching the penis and testicles with the heels, standing intent,

children.text: kiṃcid unnāmitaśirā dantair dantān na saṃspṛśet
children.translated_text: with the head somewhat raised, he should not touch tooth with tooth.
He should look at the tip of his own nose, not looking at the directions.

children.text: rajasā tamaso vṛttiṃ sattvena rajasas tathā
children.translated_text: Having covered the activity of tamas with rajas, and likewise that of rajas with sattva,

children.text: saṃchādya nirmale sattve sthito yuñjīta yogavit ||
children.translated_text: standing in stainless sattva, the knower of yoga should practice.
Having restrained the senses from the objects of the senses, and the breaths and the mind itself,
he should begin <s>pratyāhāra</s> with collectedness.

children.text: yas tu pratyāharet kāmān sarvāṅgān iva kacchapaḥ
children.translated_text: But he who withdraws desires from all his limbs, like a tortoise,
always delighting in the self and fixed in one place, sees the self in the self.
Having completed external and internal purification from the throat to the navel,
the wise man, having filled the body, should begin <s>pratyāhāra</s>.
Thus indeed, for the yogin joined with yoga, whose self is restrained,
all faults perish, and he becomes healthy.
<s>Gheraṇḍa</s> said:
Now then I shall fully teach the rule of <s>prāṇāyāma</s>,
by the mere practice of which a man becomes equal to a god.

children.text: ādau sthānaṃ tathā kālaṃ mitāhāraṃ tathāparam
children.translated_text: First, place, then time, and then moderate food besides;

children.text: nāḍīśuddhiṃ tataḥ paścāt prāṇāyāmaṃ ca sādhayet ||
children.translated_text: after that, purification of the channels; then he should practice <s>prāṇāyāma</s>.
In a distant country, in a forest, in a capital city, or near people,

children.text: yogārambhaṃ na kurvīta kṛtaś cet siddhihā bhavet ||
children.translated_text: one should not begin yoga; if it is done, it may destroy success.
In a distant country there is lack of trust; in a forest there is lack of food;

children.text: lokāraṇye prakāśaś ca tasmāt trīṇi vivarjayet ||
children.translated_text: in a populous wilderness there is publicity. Therefore one should avoid these three.
In a good country, in a righteous kingdom, with abundant food and free from disturbance,
there one should make a single hut and surround it with walls.
A pond, well, or tank should be situated within the wall,
and the hut should be neither too high nor too low, and free from insects.
The hut should be properly smeared with cow dung and free from holes.

children.text: evaṃ sthāne hi gupte ca prāṇāyāmaṃ samabhyaset ||
children.translated_text: In such a place, indeed hidden, he should practice <s>prāṇāyāma</s>.

children.text: hemante śiśire grīṣme varṣāyāṃ ca ṛtau tathā
children.translated_text: In hemanta, śiśira, summer, and also in the rainy season,

children.text: yogārambhaṃ na kurvīta kṛte yogo hi rogadaḥ ||
children.translated_text: one should not begin yoga; when begun then, yoga brings disease.
It is said that one should undertake the beginning of yoga in spring or autumn.

children.text: tadā yogo bhavet siddho rogān mukto bhaved dhruvam ||
children.translated_text: Then yoga becomes successful, and one will certainly be free from diseases.
From <s>Caitra</s> to the end of <s>Phālguna</s>, and from <s>Māgha</s> to the end of <s>Phālguna</s>,

children.text: dvau dvau māsau ṛtubhāgau anubhāvaś catuś catuḥ ||
children.translated_text: the seasonal divisions are two months each, while the experienced seasons are four months each.
Spring is <s>Caitra</s> and <s>Vaiśākha</s>; <s>Jyeṣṭha</s> and <s>Āṣāḍha</s> are summer.
The rainy season is <s>Śrāvaṇa</s> and <s>Bhādra</s>; autumn is <s>Āśvina</s> and <s>Kārttika</s>.
<s>Mārga</s> and <s>Pauṣa</s> are hemanta; <s>Māgha</s> and <s>Phālguna</s> are śiśira.
I shall explain the experienced extent of the seasons as it has been taught.
From the beginning of <s>Māgha</s> to the end of <s>Mādhava</s> is the four-month experience of spring.

children.text: caitrādi cāṣāḍhāntaṃ ca grīṣmaś cānubhavaś catuḥ
children.translated_text: From the beginning of <s>Caitra</s> to the end of <s>Āṣāḍha</s> is the four-month experience of summer.
From the beginning of <s>Āṣāḍha</s> to the end of <s>Āśvina</s> is the four-month experience of the rainy season.
From the beginning of <s>Bhādra</s> to the end of <s>Mārgaśīrṣa</s> is the four-month experience of autumn.
From the beginning of <s>Kārttika</s> to the end of <s>Māgha</s> is the four-month experience of hemanta.
They know the four months beginning with <s>Mārga</s> as the experience of śiśira.

children.text: vasante vāpi śaradi yogārambhaṃ tu samācaret
children.translated_text: One should undertake the beginning of yoga either in spring or in autumn.

children.text: tadā yogo bhavet siddho vināyāsena kathyate ||
children.translated_text: Then yoga becomes successful, and it is said to be without hardship.

children.text: mitāhāraṃ vinā yas tu yogārambhaṃ tu kārayet
children.translated_text: But he who undertakes the beginning of yoga without moderate food

children.text: nānārogo bhavet tasya kiṃcid yogo na sidhyati ||
children.translated_text: will have various diseases, and his yoga does not succeed at all.
A yogin should eat śāli rice, a barley cake, or likewise a wheat cake,
and mung beans, black gram, chickpeas and the like, clean and free from husk;

children.text: paṭolaṃ panasaṃ mānaṃ kakkolaṃ ca śukāśakam
children.translated_text: pointed gourd, jackfruit, <s>māna</s>, <s>kakkola</s>, and <s>śukāśaka</s>,
<s>drāḍhikā</s>, cucumber, plantain, fig, and <s>kaṇṭakaṇṭaka</s>,
mango-plantain, young plantain, plantain stalk, and radish,

children.text: vārttākīṃ mūlakam ṛddhiṃ yogī bhakṣaṇam ācaret ||
children.translated_text: eggplant, radish, and <s>ṛddhi</s>: these should be the yogin's food.
One should praise tender greens, kāla-greens, and likewise paṭola leaves,
the five greens, vāstūka, and hilamocikā.
Pure, very sweet, unctuous food, leaving half the belly empty,
eaten with delight in good taste: this they know as <s>mitāhāra</s> (moderate diet).

children.text: annena pūrayed ardhaṃ toyena tu tṛtīyakam
children.translated_text: One should fill half the belly with food, and a third with water;
one should preserve the fourth part of the belly for the movement of wind.

children.text: kaṭv amlaṃ lavaṇaṃ tiktaṃ bhṛṣṭaṃ ca dadhi takrakam
children.translated_text: Pungent, sour, salty, and bitter things, fried food, curds, and buttermilk,

children.text: śākotkaṭaṃ tathā madyaṃ tālaṃ ca panasaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: excessively strong greens, likewise liquor, palm fruit, and jackfruit,
horse gram, lentils, pāṇḍu, pumpkin, and stalks of greens,
bottle gourd, jujube, kapittha, thorn-apple, and palāśa,

children.text: kadambaṃ jambīraṃ bimbaṃ lakucaṃ laśunaṃ viṣam
children.translated_text: kadamba, citron, bimba, lakuca, garlic, poison,
star fruit, piyāla, asafoetida, śālmalī, and kemuka,
at the beginning of yoga one should avoid travel, women, and service of fire.

children.text: navanītaṃ ghṛtaṃ kṣīraṃ guḍaṃ śarkarādi caikṣavam ||
children.translated_text: Fresh butter, ghee, milk, molasses, sugar, and products of sugarcane,
ripe plantain, coconut, pomegranate, and aśiva-āsava,

children.text: drākṣāṃ tu lavalīṃ dhātrīṃ rasam amlavivarjitam ||
children.translated_text: grapes, lavalī, dhātrī, and juice free from sourness,
cardamom, nutmeg, cloves, pauruṣa, jambu, and jāmbala,

children.text: harītakīṃ kharjūraṃ ca yogī bhakṣaṇam ācaret ||
children.translated_text: harītakī and dates: the yogin should take these as food.
Food that digests lightly, is agreeable, unctuous, and nourishes the bodily constituents,
desired by the mind and suitable: the yogin should take such food.

children.text: kāṭhinyaṃ duritaṃ pūtim uṣṇaṃ paryuṣitaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Hard, bad, putrid, hot, and stale food,

children.text: atiśītaṃ cāti coṣṇaṃ bhakṣyaṃ yogī vivarjayet ||
children.translated_text: too cold and also too hot: the yogin should avoid such things to be eaten.
Morning bathing, fasting, and the like, and any rule that torments the body,

children.text: ekāhāraṃ nirāhāraṃ yāmānte ca na kārayet ||
children.translated_text: one meal a day, no meal at all, and eating only at the end of a watch: he should not practice these.
In this way, according to the prescribed rule, he should undertake <s>prāṇāyāma</s>.
At the first beginning he should make milk and the like his daily food;
at midday and in the evening he should take two meals.
On a seat of kuśa grass, on an antelope skin, on a tiger skin, or on a blanket,
seated on a thick seat, facing east or else facing north,
having attained purification of the nāḍīs, he should properly practice <s>prāṇāyāma</s>.
<s>Caṇḍakāpāli</s> said:

children.text: nāḍīśuddhiṃ kathaṃ kuryān nāḍīśuddhis tu kīdṛśī
children.translated_text: How should one perform purification of the nāḍīs, and what is nāḍī purification like?

children.text: tat sarvaṃ śrotum icchāmi tad vadasva dayānidhe ||
children.translated_text: I wish to hear all that; tell it, ocean of compassion.
<s>Gheraṇḍa</s> said:
When the nāḍīs are full of impurity, the wind does not move at all.

children.text: prāṇāyāmaḥ kathaṃ sidhyet tattvajñānaṃ kathaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: How could <s>prāṇāyāma</s> be accomplished, and how could knowledge of reality arise?
Therefore one should first practice nāḍī purification, and after that <s>prāṇāyāma</s>.

children.text: nāḍīśuddhir dvidhā proktā samanur nirmanus tathā
children.translated_text: Nāḍī purification is taught as twofold: with mantra and without mantra.
One should perform the mantra-based kind with a seed syllable, and the non-mantra kind by the cleansing acts.
The cleansing act has been taught before, as in the practice of the six acts.

children.text: śṛṇuṣva samanuṃ caṇḍa nāḍīśuddhir yathā bhavet ||
children.translated_text: Listen to the mantra-based kind, <s>Caṇḍa</s>, by which nāḍī purification comes about.
Having sat down on a seat, the yogin should assume the lotus posture.
Having performed the nyāsa beginning with the guru, exactly as taught by the guru,
he should perform nāḍī purification for the purification of <s>prāṇāyāma</s>.
Then, meditating on the wind seed syllable, smoky-colored and radiant,

children.text: candreṇa pūrayed vāyuṃ bījaṃ ṣoḍaśakaiḥ sudhīḥ ||
children.translated_text: the wise man should draw in the wind through the moon channel with sixteen repetitions of the seed.
He should hold it with kumbhaka for sixty-four measures,
and should exhale the wind through the sun nāḍī for thirty-two measures.
Raising fire from the root of the navel, he should meditate on radiance joined with earth;
with the fire seed, in sixteen measures, he should inhale through the sun nāḍī.
He should hold it with kumbhaka for sixty-four measures,
and should exhale the wind through the moon nāḍī for thirty-two measures.
Having meditated at the tip of the nose on the moon-bearing disk, endowed with moonlight,

children.text: ṭhaṃ bījaṃ ṣoḍaśenaiva iḍayā pūrayen marut ||
children.translated_text: with the seed syllable <s>ṭhaṃ</s>, in sixteen measures, he should draw in the breath through <s>iḍā</s>.
He should hold it with kumbhaka for sixty-four measures,
and, meditating on himself as flooded with nectar, he should practice <s>prāṇāyāma</s>.

children.text: evaṃ bījaṃ ṣoḍaśenaiva sūryanāḍyā ca pūrayet
children.translated_text: In this way, with the seed in sixteen measures, he should inhale through the sun nāḍī,
and, with the letter <s>la</s> for thirty-two, having firmly visualized, he should exhale.
Having performed nāḍī purification of this kind, he should purify the nāḍī.
Becoming firm and assuming the posture, he should practice <s>prāṇāyāma</s>.

children.text: sahitaḥ sūryabhedaś ca ujjāyī śītalī tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Sahita</s>, <s>sūryabheda</s>, <s>ujjāyī</s>, <s>śītalī</s>,

children.text: bhastrikā bhrāmarī mūrchā kevalī cāṣṭa kumbhikāḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>bhastrikā</s>, <s>bhrāmarī</s>, <s>mūrchā</s>, and <s>kevalī</s>: these are the eight kumbhakas.
The two kinds of <s>sahita</s> have been taught; he should practice <s>prāṇāyāma</s>.
The seed is uttered in the seed-filled form, while the seedless form is without the seed.

children.text: prāṇāyāmaṃ sagarbhaṃ ca prathamaṃ kathayāmi te ||
children.translated_text: First I shall explain to you the seed-filled <s>prāṇāyāma</s>.
Having sat comfortably, facing east or else facing north,
he should meditate on <s>Vidhi</s>, composed of the quality of passion, red in color, with the letter <s>a</s>.

children.text: iḍayā pūrayed vāyuṃ mātrayā ṣoḍaśaiḥ sudhīḥ
children.translated_text: The wise man should draw in the wind through <s>iḍā</s> for sixteen measures.
At the end of inhalation and the beginning of kumbhaka, <s>uḍḍīyānaka</s> should be performed.
Meditating on <s>Hari</s>, consisting of sattva, with white-colored syllables <s>u</s>,

children.text: catuḥṣaṣṭyā ca mātrayā anilaṃ kumbhakaṃ caret
children.translated_text: he should perform kumbhaka of the breath for sixty-four measures.
At the end of kumbhaka and the beginning of exhalation, <s>jālaṃdhara</s> should be performed.
Meditating on <s>Rudra</s>, the quality of darkness, with black-colored syllables <s>m</s>,
he should then exhale again according to rule for thirty-two measures.
Again, filling through <s>piṅgalā</s>, he should hold it with kumbhaka,

children.text: iḍayā recayet paścāt tadbījena krameṇa tu ||
children.translated_text: and afterward exhale through <s>iḍā</s>, in sequence with that seed syllable.
He should practice again and again in the forward and reverse order.
At the end of inhalation, at the beginning of retention, the two nostril openings are held
with the little finger, ring finger, and thumb, without using the index and middle fingers.

children.text: prāṇāyāmaṃ nigarbhaṃ tu vinā bījena jāyate
children.translated_text: But prāṇāyāma without a seed-syllable arises as the seedless kind.
One should move the left palm placed upon the left knee,
with inhalation, retention, and exhalation up to one hundred mātrās and so on.

children.text: uttamā viṃśatir mātrā madhyamā ṣoḍaśī smṛtā
children.translated_text: Twenty mātrās are the highest; sixteen are remembered as middling;

children.text: adhamā dvādaśī mātrā prāṇāyāmās tridhā smṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: twelve mātrās are the lowest. Prāṇāyāmas are remembered as threefold.

children.text: adhamāj jāyate gharmo merukampaś ca madhyamāt
children.translated_text: From the lowest comes sweat; from the middling comes trembling of the spine;
and from the highest comes leaving the ground. This is the threefold mark of accomplishment.
From prāṇāyāma comes the state of moving in the sky; from prāṇāyāma comes the destruction of disease.
From prāṇāyāma one should awaken the śakti; from prāṇāyāma comes <s>manonmanī</s>.

children.text: ānando jāyate citte prāṇāyāmī sukhī bhavet ||
children.translated_text: Bliss arises in the mind, and the practitioner of prāṇāyāma becomes happy.
The <s>sahita kumbha</s> has been explained; now hear the <s>sūryabhedana</s>.
One should fill oneself with the outer air through the solar channel, according to one's strength.
With great effort one should hold it by retention together with the <s>jalaṃdhara</s> locks,

children.text: yāvat svedaṃ nakhakeśābhyāṃ tāvat kurvantu kumbhakam ||
children.translated_text: and they should perform retention until sweat appears from the nails and hair.
<s>Prāṇa</s>, <s>apāna</s>, <s>samāna</s>, and also <s>udāna</s> and <s>vyāna</s> are the winds;

children.text: nāgaḥ kūrmaś ca kṛkaro devadatto dhanaṃjayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>nāga</s>, <s>kūrma</s>, <s>kṛkara</s>, <s>devadatta</s>, and <s>dhanaṃjaya</s> are also such.

children.text: hṛdi prāṇo vahen nityam apāno gudamaṇḍale
children.translated_text: <s>Prāṇa</s> always moves in the heart; <s>apāna</s> is in the anal region.
<s>Samāna</s> is in the region of the navel, while <s>udāna</s> is situated in the middle of the throat.

children.text: vyāno vyāpya śarīre tu pradhānāḥ pañca vāyavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vyāna</s> pervades the body; these are the five principal winds.

children.text: prāṇādyāḥ pañca vikhyātā nāgādyāḥ pañca vāyavaḥ
children.translated_text: The five beginning with <s>prāṇa</s> are famous, and the five beginning with <s>nāga</s> are also winds.

children.text: teṣām api ca pañcānāṃ sthānāni ca vadāmy aham ||
children.translated_text: Now I shall tell the places of those five as well.

children.text: udgāre nāga ākhyātaḥ kūrmas tūnmīlane smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Nāga</s> is said to be in belching; <s>kūrma</s> is remembered in opening the eyes.
<s>Kṛkara</s> is known in hunger and thirst, and <s>devadatta</s> in yawning.

children.text: na jahāti mṛte kvāpi sarvavyāpī dhanaṃjayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s>, all-pervading, never departs anywhere even when one is dead.

children.text: nāgo gṛhṇāti caitanyaṃ kūrmaś caiva nimeṣaṇam
children.translated_text: <s>Nāga</s> takes hold of consciousness, and <s>kūrma</s> brings blinking.

children.text: kṣuttṛṣaṃ kṛkaraś caiva jṛmbhaṇaṃ caturthena tu
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛkara</s> brings hunger and thirst, and yawning comes through the fourth.

children.text: bhaved dhanaṃjayāc chabdaṃ kṣaṇamātraṃ na niḥsaret ||
children.translated_text: Through <s>dhanaṃjaya</s> sound may arise, and it does not go out for even a moment.

children.text: sarvaṃ ca sūryakaṃ bhitvā nābhimūlāt samuddharet ||
children.translated_text: Having pierced all the solar channel, one should raise it up from the root of the navel.
Afterward one should exhale through <s>iḍā</s>, steadily and with unbroken force.
Again, drawing it in through the solar channel and retaining it according to rule,

children.text: recayitvā sādhayet tu krameṇa ca punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: then exhaling, one should practice it gradually again and again.
This retention is <s>sūryabheda</s>, destroying old age and death.
It awakens the <s>kuṇḍalī śakti</s> and increases the bodily fire.

children.text: iti te kathitaṃ caṇḍa sūryabhedanam uttamam ||
children.translated_text: Thus, <s>Caṇḍa</s>, the excellent <s>sūryabhedana</s> has been taught to you.

children.text: nāsābhyāṃ vāyum ākṛṣya mukhamadhye ca dhārayet
children.translated_text: Drawing in the air through the two nostrils, one should hold it in the middle of the mouth.
Drawing the air together through the heart and throat, one should hold it with the mouth.

children.text: mukhaṃ praphullaṃ saṃrakṣya kuryāj jālaṃdharaṃ tataḥ
children.translated_text: Keeping the mouth expanded, one should then perform <s>jālaṃdhara</s>.
Having made retention according to one's strength, one should hold it without strain.
Having performed <s>ujjāyī kumbhaka</s>, one may accomplish all undertakings.

children.text: na bhavet kapharogaś ca krūravāyur ajīrṇakam ||
children.translated_text: Phlegmatic disease, harsh wind, and indigestion do not arise.

children.text: āmavātaḥ kṣayaḥ kāso jvaraplīhā na jāyate
children.translated_text: Rheumatic disease, consumption, cough, fever, and spleen disease do not arise.
A man should practice <s>ujjāyī</s> for the destruction of old age and death.

children.text: jihvayā vāyum ākṛṣya udare pūrayec chanaiḥ
children.translated_text: Drawing in air with the tongue, one should slowly fill the belly.

children.text: kṣaṇaṃ ca kumbhakaṃ kṛtvā nāsābhyāṃ recayet punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having retained it for a moment, one should exhale again through the two nostrils.
The yogin should always practice the auspicious <s>śītalī kumbhaka</s>.

children.text: ajīrṇaṃ kaphapittaṃ ca naiva tasya prajāyate
children.translated_text: Indigestion, phlegm, and bile never arise for him.

children.text: tato vāyuṃ ca nāsābhyām ubhābhyāṃ cālayec chanaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then one should slowly move the air through both nostrils.

children.text: evaṃ viṃśativāraṃ ca kṛtvā kuryācca kumbhakam
children.translated_text: Having done this twenty times, one should then perform retention.

children.text: tadante cālayed vāyuṃ pūrvoktaṃ ca yathāvidhi ||
children.translated_text: At its end one should move the air in the manner previously stated.
The wise man should practice this <s>bhastrikā kumbhaka</s> three times.

children.text: na ca rogo na ca kleśa ārogyaṃ ca dine dine ||
children.translated_text: There is no disease and no affliction; health increases day by day.
When midnight has passed, when the sounds of living beings have ceased,

children.text: karṇau nidhāya hastābhyāṃ kuryāt pūrakam uttamam ||
children.translated_text: the yogin should close his ears with his hands and perform the excellent inhalation.

children.text: śṛṇuyād dakṣiṇe karṇe nādam antargataṃ sudhīḥ
children.translated_text: The wise man should hear the internal sound in the right ear.

children.text: prathamaṃ jhiñjhīnādaṃ ca vaṃśīnādaṃ tataḥ param
children.translated_text: First there is the sound of crickets, then the sound of a flute;
after that, the rumbling of clouds, the buzzing of bees, and the sound of a bell and bronze vessel.
Then come the sounds of trumpet, kettledrum, mṛdaṅga, battle-drum, kettledrum, and dundubhi.

children.text: evaṃ nānāvidho nādo jāyate nityam abhyāsāt ||
children.translated_text: Thus, from constant practice, many kinds of sound arise.

children.text: anāhatasya śabdasya tasya śabdasya yo dhvaniḥ
children.translated_text: That sound is the resonance of the unstruck sound.
Within the resonance is light, and within the light is the mind.

children.text: tasmiṃs tu vilayaṃ yāti tad viṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam
children.translated_text: When it dissolves there, that is the supreme abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
Thus perfection in <s>bhrāmarī</s> obtains perfection in samādhi.

children.text: mukhe ca kumbhakaṃ kṛtvā bhruvor antargataṃ manaḥ
children.translated_text: Having made retention in the mouth, with the mind placed between the eyebrows,
and abandoning all objects of sense, <s>manomūrchā</s> is a giver of happiness.
From the union of the mind with the self, bliss surely arises.
Thus many kinds of bliss arise from constant practice.
In this way, through the yoga of practice, one obtains perfection in samādhi.
Through the breath-control of <s>bhujaṅginī</s>, indeed, the unrecited recitation arises.

children.text: haṃkāreṇa bahir yāti saḥkāreṇa viśet punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: It goes out with the sound <s>haṃ</s> and enters again with the sound <s>saḥ</s>.
Six hundred by day and night, and twenty-one thousand,

children.text: ajapāṃ nāma gāyatrīṃ jīvo japati sarvadā ||
children.translated_text: the living being always recites the <s>gāyatrī</s> called <s>ajapā</s>.

children.text: mūlādhāre yathā haṃsas tathā hi hṛdi paṅkaje
children.translated_text: As the <s>haṃsa</s> is in the <s>mūlādhāra</s>, so indeed it is in the lotus of the heart,
and likewise in the pair of nostrils, at the coming to the confluence of the three streams.
The body, measuring ninety-six finger-breadths, is formed of action.
The breath that has gone outside the body is naturally twelve finger-breadths.
When lying down it is sixteen finger-breadths, and likewise twenty when eating;
on the road it is twenty-four finger-breadths, in sleep thirty finger-breadths;

children.text: maithune ṣaṭtriṃśad uktaṃ vyāyāme ca tato 'dhikam ||
children.translated_text: in sexual intercourse it is said to be thirty-six, and in exercise still more than that.

children.text: svabhāve 'sya gater nyūne param āyuḥ pravardhate
children.translated_text: When its movement is less than its natural measure, the full span of life increases;
when the wind has entered inward beyond that, loss of life-span is declared.

children.text: tasmāt prāṇe sthite dehe maraṇaṃ naiva jāyate
children.translated_text: Therefore, while the prāṇa remains in the body, death does not occur at all.
When the pot-like body is joined with the breath, there is <s>kevalakumbhaka</s> (absolute breath retention).
As long as he lives, he should recite the mantra, only according to the number of the unrecited ajapā.
Until now a confusion of counting has been maintained, once it has been made kevalī.

children.text: ata eva hi kartavyaḥ kevalīkumbhako naraiḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore <s>kevalīkumbhaka</s> should indeed be performed by men.
<s>Kevalī</s>, the number of ajapā, and the mind-transcending state are doubled.

children.text: nāsābhyāṃ vāyum ākṛṣya kevalaṃ kumbhakaṃ caret
children.translated_text: Drawing in the breath through the two nostrils, one should practice only kumbhaka.
On the first day he should hold it from one up to sixty-four counts.

children.text: kevalīm aṣṭadhā kuryād yāme yāme dine dine
children.translated_text: Day by day, in every watch of the day, he should perform <s>kevalī</s> eight times;

children.text: athavā pañcadhā kuryād yathā tat kathayāmi te ||
children.translated_text: or else he should do it five times, as I shall tell you.
In the morning, at midday, in the evening, and fourthly at midnight,

children.text: trisaṃdhyam athavā kuryāt samamāne dine dine ||
children.translated_text: or else he should practice it at the three junctions of the day, in equal measure day by day.

children.text: pañcavāraṃ dine vṛddhir vāraikaṃ ca dine tathā
children.translated_text: There should be an increase of five times in a day, or one time in a day likewise,
until accomplishment arises in the measure of ajapā.

children.text: prāṇāyāmaṃ kevalīṃ nāma tadā vadati yogavit
children.translated_text: Then the knower of yoga calls that prāṇāyāma by the name <s>kevalī</s>.

children.text: kumbhake kevale siddhe kiṃ na sidhyati bhūtale ||
children.translated_text: When pure kumbhaka has been mastered, what is there on earth that is not accomplished?
<s>Gheraṇḍa</s> said:

children.text: sthūlaṃ jyotis tathā sūkṣmaṃ dhyānasya trividhaṃ viduḥ
children.translated_text: They know meditation to be threefold: gross, luminous, and subtle.

children.text: sthūlaṃ mūrtimayaṃ proktaṃ jyotis tejomayaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: The gross is said to consist of formed images, and the luminous to consist of radiance;
