the subtle is <s>Brahman</s> consisting of bindu, <s>Kuṇḍalī</s>, the supreme deity.
In his own heart he should meditate on an excellent ocean of nectar;
in its midst, on a jewel island made of excellent jeweled sand;
in the four directions, on kadamba trees furnished with many flowers,
as if surrounded all around by dense groves of kadamba trees;
with mālatī, mallikā, jātī, kesara, and campaka flowers,
with pārijāta and land-lotuses, whose fragrance perfumes the quarters.
In the midst of that the yogin should call to mind a charming wish-fulfilling tree,
with four branches as the four Vedas, always furnished with flowers and fruits.

children.text: bhramarāḥ kokilās tatra guñjanti nigadanti ca
children.translated_text: There bees hum and cuckoos sing.
Having become steady, he should meditate there on a great pavilion of ruby.

children.text: tanmadhye tu smared yogī paryaṅkaṃ sumanoharam
children.translated_text: In its midst the yogin should call to mind a very charming couch.
There he should meditate on his chosen deity, according to the meditation taught by the guru.

children.text: yasya devasya yad rūpaṃ yathā bhūṣaṇavāhanam
children.translated_text: Whatever the form of that deity is, and whatever its ornaments and vehicle are,

children.text: tad rūpaṃ dhyāyate nityaṃ sthūladhyānam idaṃ viduḥ ||
children.translated_text: he constantly meditates on that form; this they know as gross meditation.
In the great thousand-petaled lotus, in the pericarp, he should contemplate
a lotus with its filaments attached, furnished with twelve petals.
It is white in color, greatly radiant, and expressed by twelve seed-syllables:
sa, ha, kṣa, ma, va, la, ra, ya, uṃ, and the haṃsa-śakti, in due order.
In its middle, in the pericarp, there are the three lines beginning with a, ka, and tha;
there is the praṇava, joined with the triangle of ha, la, and kṣa.
There he should meditate on a charming seat made of nāda and bindu.
Above it is the pair of haṃsas; there are the sandals there.

children.text: dhyāyet tatra guruṃ devaṃ vibhujaṃ ca trilocanam
children.translated_text: There he should meditate on the divine guru, two-armed and three-eyed,
the god wearing white garments and anointed with white sandal paste,
with a garland made of white flowers, accompanied by red śakti.
Through meditation on the guru in this form, gross meditation is perfected.

children.text: kathitaṃ sthūladhyānaṃ tu tejodhyānaṃ śṛṇuṣva me
children.translated_text: Gross meditation has been taught; now hear from me luminous meditation.

children.text: yad dhyānena yogasiddhir ātmapratyakṣam eva ca
children.translated_text: By meditation on it there is yogic accomplishment and direct perception of the self.
In the mūlādhāra is <s>Kuṇḍalinī</s>, whose form is like a serpent.
There the individual self remains, in the form of a lamp-flame.

children.text: dhyāyet tejomayaṃ brahma tejodhyānaṃ tad eva hi ||
children.translated_text: He should meditate on radiant <s>Brahman</s>; that indeed is luminous meditation.
At the root of the navel is the sun.

children.text: dhyāyet tejo mahad vyāptaṃ tejodhyānaṃ tad eva hi ||
children.translated_text: He should meditate on a great, all-pervading radiance; that indeed is luminous meditation.

children.text: bhruvor madhye manordhve ca yat tejaḥ praṇavātmakam
children.translated_text: Between the eyebrows and above the mind, that radiance whose nature is praṇava

children.text: dhyāyej jvālāvalīyuktaṃ tejodhyānaṃ tad eva hi ||
children.translated_text: he should meditate on as joined with a mass of flames; that indeed is luminous meditation.

children.text: tejodhyānaṃ śrutaṃ caṇḍa sūkṣmadhyānaṃ vadāmy aham
children.translated_text: You have heard luminous meditation, <s>Caṇḍa</s>; I shall speak of subtle meditation.
By the force of great good fortune, one's <s>Kuṇḍalī</s> may become awakened.
United with the self through yoga, she goes out through the aperture of the eyes.

children.text: vihared rājamārge ca cañcalatvān na dṛśyate ||
children.translated_text: She moves along the royal road, and because of her swiftness she is not seen.
Through <s>śāmbhavīmudrā</s>, the yogin succeeds by the yoga of meditation.

children.text: sūkṣmadhyānam idaṃ gopyaṃ devānām api durlabham ||
children.translated_text: This subtle meditation is secret, hard even for the gods to obtain.
Luminous meditation is declared to be a hundred times greater than gross meditation;
subtle meditation is a hundred thousand times greater than luminous meditation, supreme beyond the highest.

children.text: iti te kathitaṃ caṇḍa dhyānayogaṃ sudurlabham
children.translated_text: Thus, <s>Caṇḍa</s>, the very difficult yoga of meditation has been taught to you.

children.text: ātmā sākṣād bhaved yasmāt tasmād dhyānaṃ viśiṣyate ||
children.translated_text: Since through it the self becomes directly manifest, meditation is therefore distinguished.
<s>Gheraṇḍa</s> said:
<s>Samādhi</s> too is the supreme reality, obtained through abundant good fortune.
It is attained through the grace and favor of the guru, and through devotion to the guru.
Knowledge of the teaching, trust in one's own guru, realization of the self, and awakening of the mind:

children.text: dine dine yasya bhavet sa yogī suśobhanābhyāsam upaiti sadyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the yogin for whom these arise day by day immediately attains very beautiful practice.

children.text: ghaṭād bhinnaṃ manaḥ kṛtvā aikyaṃ kuryāt parātmani
children.translated_text: Having made the mind separate from the body, one should unite it with the supreme self.
One should know that to be <s>samādhi</s>; by its stages and so on one is known as liberated.

children.text: ahaṃ brahma na cānyo 'smi brahmaivāhaṃ na śokabhāk
children.translated_text: I am <s>Brahman</s>, and I am no other; I am <s>Brahman</s> alone, not one who partakes of grief.
I am of the nature of being, consciousness, and bliss, eternally liberated and possessed of my own true nature.
By <s>śāmbhavī</s>, by <s>khecarī</s>, by <s>bhrāmarī</s>, and by <s>yonimudrā</s>,
there are four accomplishments: meditation, sound, the bliss of rasa, and absorption.
With <s>bhaktiyoga</s> as the fifth, and <s>manomūrchā</s> as the sixth,
this <s>rājayoga</s> is sixfold; understand each one separately.
Having performed the <s>śāmbhavī</s> seal, one should bring about direct perception of the self.
Seeing the bindu as consisting of <s>Brahman</s>, one should fix the mind there.

children.text: khamadhye kuru cātmānam ātmamadhye ca khaṃ kuru
children.translated_text: Place the self in the midst of space, and place space in the midst of the self.

children.text: ātmānaṃ khamayaṃ dṛṣṭvā na kiṃcid api bādhyate
children.translated_text: Seeing the self as made of space, one is not obstructed by anything at all.
Having become full of eternal bliss, a person should become established in <s>samādhi</s>.
When, through the practice of <s>khecarīmudrā</s>, the tongue has gone upward,
then the accomplishment of <s>samādhi</s> arises, after ordinary action has been abandoned.
With a gentle speed one should practice <s>bhrāmarī kumbhaka</s> with the breath.

children.text: mandaṃ mandaṃ recayed vāyuṃ bhṛṅganādaṃ tato bhavet ||
children.translated_text: One should exhale the breath very gently; then the sound of a bee arises.

children.text: antaḥsthaṃ bhramarīnādaṃ śrutvā tatra mano nayet
children.translated_text: Having heard the inner <s>bhrāmarī</s> sound, one should lead the mind there.

children.text: samādhir jāyate tatra ānandaḥ so 'ham ity ataḥ ||
children.translated_text: There <s>samādhi</s> is born, and bliss arises from the thought 'I am that.'
Having attained <s>yonimudrā</s>, one should oneself become made of <s>śakti</s>.
Through the rasa of excellent erotic delight, one should sport in the supreme self.
Having become full of bliss, one comes into unity with <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: ahaṃ brahmeti cādvaitaṃ samādhis tena jāyate ||
children.translated_text: Through the non-dual realization 'I am <s>Brahman</s>,' <s>samādhi</s> is thereby born.
In one's own heart one should meditate on the form of one's chosen deity.
Through <s>bhaktiyoga</s>, one should contemplate it with supreme joy.
With tears of bliss and horripilation, the state of devotional emotion arises.

children.text: samādhiḥ sambhavet tena sambhavec ca manonmanī ||
children.translated_text: Through that, <s>samādhi</s> may arise, and <s>manonmanī</s> may also arise.
Having attained <s>manomūrchā</s>, one should join the mind to the self.
Through union with the supreme self, one may obtain <s>samādhi</s>.

children.text: iti te kathitaṃ caṇḍa samādhir muktilakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Thus, <s>Caṇḍa</s>, <s>samādhi</s>, whose mark is liberation, has been taught to you.

children.text: rājayogaḥ samādhiḥ syād ekātmany eva sādhanam
children.translated_text: <s>Rājayoga</s> is <s>samādhi</s>; it is a practice solely in the one self.
<s>Unmanī</s> and the natural state are all terms denoting the one self.

children.text: jale viṣṇuḥ sthale viṣṇur viṣṇuḥ parvatamastake
children.translated_text: <s>Viṣṇu</s> is in water, <s>Viṣṇu</s> is on land, and <s>Viṣṇu</s> is on the summit of a mountain.
<s>Viṣṇu</s> is amid masses of flames; the whole world is made of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
All these living beings, as many as there are, moving on earth and moving in the sky,
trees, shrubs, creepers, vines, grasses and the like, waters and mountains:

children.text: sarvaṃ brahma vijānīyāt sarvaṃ paśyati cātmani ||
children.translated_text: one should know all of it as <s>Brahman</s>; one sees all in the self.
The self is the consciousness situated in the body, non-dual, eternal, and supreme.
Knowledge that is altogether distinct from the body is free from passion and without latent impressions.
Such is <s>samādhi</s>, devoid of all conceptual constructions.
Toward one's own body, sons, wife and other relatives, wealth and the rest,
having become without possessiveness toward all these, one may obtain <s>samādhi</s>.

children.text: layāmṛtaṃ paraṃ tattvaṃ śivoktaṃ vividhāni ca
children.translated_text: The nectar of absorption, the supreme reality, and the various teachings spoken by <s>Śiva</s>:
taking their essence in brief, I have taught what has liberation as its mark.
